description: Engine files that print the cart's own text by label through data.text (src/core/RomText.lua), which mod.content.rom_text overrides on Gen 2. The scope is every label of the extracted rom_text catalog named in these files' code. `slots` says how the reader fills the text's {MARKERS}: `named` readers substitute them by name, so a translation may reorder them, drop one, or name the battler the engine always passes; `exact` readers print the text as stored, so a translation keeps the English markers in order. `anchors` replaces the corpus row a label would join by its own name, per language, where the corpus places that label's text elsewhere. This file contains selectors only, never translated prose.

src/battle/gen2.why: Battle:romText fills {USER} and {TARGET} with the battlers it is always given, {STRBUF} and {NUM} with the value it is passed (src/battle/gen2/Battle.lua).

src/script/gen2/specials/battle_tower.lu.why: The Battle Tower's entry rules are shown as RomText returns them; the script VM fills {STRBUF} itself.

src/ui/gen2/GenderSelect.lua.why: Crystal's gender question is printed as RomText returns it.

src/ui/gen2/union/Text.lua.why: The Union Room's cancelled-link line is read straight from data.text.

InLoveWithText.why: The Korean cart's battle text sits one label later than the English around the infatuation messages: InLoveWithText's own row is the ENDURE line, InfatuationText's row is the falling-in-love line.

InfatuationText.why: Same shift: DisabledMoveText's Korean row is the infatuation-kept-it-from-attacking line.

DisabledMoveText.why: Same shift: LoafingAroundText's Korean row is the move-is-disabled line.
